name: Rwandan Isombe
description: Isombe, pounded cassava leaves simmered with eggplant and peanuts, is one of Rwanda's most beloved dishes - real cassava leaves aren't a distinct item here, so spinach stands in for a milder, less fibrous approximation.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion and eggplant 6-7 minutes.
Whisk in the peanut butter with a little water, then add the spinach.
Simmer 15-18 minutes until well combined.

name: Rwandan Ugali (Ubugali)
description: Ubugali, a stiff maize or cassava porridge, is Rwanda's most essential staple starch, closely related to ugali found across much of East Africa.
steps_detailed: Whisk the cornmeal into 1.25 cups boiling water.

name: Rwandan Brochettes
description: Brochettes, grilled skewered meat, is one of Rwanda's most beloved foods, commonly goat but made here with beef, a widely available protein with a similarly hearty character.
steps_detailed: Marinate the beef in the garlic and oil for 15-20 minutes.
Thread onto skewers and grill, turning, 8-10 minutes, until charred and cooked through.

name: Rwandan Ibirayi n'Imboga (Potatoes and Greens)
description: Potatoes cooked together with leafy greens, a genuine Rwandan staple reflecting the country's fertile, hilly agricultural land.
steps_detailed: Boil the potato until just tender, 12-15 minutes.
Cook the onion 4-5 minutes, then add the kale and simmer 10-12 minutes.
Combine the potato with the kale mixture.

name: Rwandan Sombe with Fish
description: A fish-based variation of Rwanda's beloved isombe greens dish, real spinach standing in for cassava leaves.

Whisk the peanut butter with a little water, add the spinach and flaked fish.
Simmer 12-15 minutes until well combined.

name: Rwandan Chapati
description: Chapati, a soft, layered flatbread, reflects genuine East African Indian culinary influence and is a beloved Rwandan bread.
steps_detailed: Work the flour with warm water and half the oil into a soft dough. Rest 20 minutes.
Roll thin, brush with the remaining oil, and coil before flattening to build real layers.
Cook in a hot, dry pan, 2-3 minutes per side, until golden.
